# Multiple document references per smartphrase — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

*Generated by 'superpowers' plugin v6.3.0 (superpowers@claude-plugins-official)*

**Goal:** Replace single-valued `sapRef` and first-match-wins anchor resolution with plural `sapRefs[]` and a union-plus-ranking resolver, so a phrase use carries every passage that grounds it and leads with the one specifying the analysis being inspected.

**Architecture:** All resolution lives in one exported engine function, `anchorForPhrase`, which both the prose projection and the JSON-LD projection already share — that sharing is the invariant that stops the two disagreeing about provenance, and it must survive. Ranking keys are level, then section proximity to the analysis's own section, then an optional authored `relation`, then declaration order. The verification gates assert the ranking on live study data, not on fixtures alone.

**Tech Stack:** Plain ES5-style browser JavaScript (`demo/*.js`, `demo/index.html` — loaded by `<script src>` from `file://`, no build step), Node ESM for tooling (`tools/*.mjs`), jsdom for the headless DOM gate, JSON goldens for regression.

**Spec:** [.sdlc/change-docs/specs/issue-13-multiple-references-spec.md](../specs/issue-13-multiple-references-spec.md) — read it first; this plan argues from it and does not repeat its reasoning.

**Issue:** [#13](https://github.com/cdisc-org/analysis-concepts/issues/13) · **Branch:** `dev/metadatadriven/issue-13-multiple-references`

## Global Constraints

Every task's requirements implicitly include these.

- **Zero-install.** Static files opened over `file://`. No `fetch`, no bundler, no build step, no `npm install`. `demo/*.js` are IIFEs attaching to `window` (or `globalThis` under Node).
- **ES5-style browser JavaScript in `demo/`.** Use `var` and `function`. No arrow functions, no template literals, no `const`/`let`, no spread. `Object.assign` and `Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter/some/reduce` are in use already and are fine. `tools/*.mjs` is modern Node ESM and has no such restriction.
- **The library wall.** Library entities — methods, output classes, transformation templates, `demo/data/acdc-library.js`, `demo/data/acdc-library-proposed.js` — MUST NOT carry study text. Every change in this plan is study-side or engine-side. `acdc-library.js` is generated and must never be hand-edited.
- **Goldens are captured from behaviour, never hand-written.** Recapture with `--update-goldens`, then review the movement with `diff-goldens.mjs`. Never edit `tools/goldens.json` by hand.
- **Identifier policy.** Ground into USDM / ARS / STATO / NCIt where a term covers the entity; anything else carries `iri_status: "illustrative"`. Never invent a plausible-looking registered identifier.
- **British English** in all prose, comments and documentation. Note that quoted SAP text is American English and is reproduced verbatim — never "correct" a quotation.
- **Commits** reference `#13` in the subject line and carry the trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Commit with `git commit -F <file>` using a heredoc, because backticks in a `-m` argument are executed by the shell.

## Test commands

There is no test framework and no `package.json`. The gates are scripts, run from the repository root:

```bash
node smartphrase/tools/verify.mjs                  # engine + goldens gate
node smartphrase/tools/verify.mjs --update-goldens  # recapture goldens
node smartphrase/tools/verify-ui.mjs                # headless DOM gate (jsdom)
node smartphrase/tools/diff-goldens.mjs --summary    # review golden movement vs HEAD
```

"Write the failing test" in this plan means **add an assertion to `verify.mjs` or `verify-ui.mjs` and run it**. That is this repository's test idiom and TDD applies to it normally.

## Task 1: Plural shape, zero behaviour change

Migrate every anchor site from `sapRef: {…}` to `sapRefs: [{…}]` and make every reader list-aware, while keeping first-match-wins resolution exactly as it is. Nothing about *which* passage is chosen changes in this task. That is what makes it independently reviewable: the golden diff must show renamed fields and nothing else.

- Produces: `refsOf(x) → Array` (engine-internal); `anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def) → { anchors: Array, anchor: Object|null, source: String|null }`; every study-side entity carries `sapRefs: Array` in place of `sapRef: Object`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the `refsOf` normaliser to `engine.js`**

Insert immediately above `anchorForPhrase` (before the comment block at line 228):

```js
  /*
   * Every study-side anchor site is a LIST (issue #13). A concept exists to be
   * reused, and the analyses that bind it are specified in different sections,
   * so one reference can never be the right anchor for all of them.
   *
   * Absent and empty are different answers: an absent sapRefs is an unanswered
   * question, whereas [] states "nothing in the document grounds this" and must
   * be accompanied by noAnchorReason. Both read as no references here; the gate
   * is what distinguishes them.
   */
  function refsOf(x) {
    return (x && x.sapRefs) || [];
  }
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Make `anchorForPhrase` list-aware, preserving first-match-wins**

Replace the body of `anchorForPhrase` (lines 244–254). Keep the existing comment block above it untouched in this task.

```js
  function anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def) {
    var own = refsOf(pi);
    if (own.length) {
      return { anchors: own.slice(), anchor: own[0], source: "phraseInstance" };
    }
    var found = null;
    ((def && def.placeholders) || []).some(function (ph) {
      var b = (pi.bindings || {})[ph.name];
      var c = b && b.concept && concept(ctx, b.concept);
      var refs = refsOf(c);
      if (refs.length) {
        found = { anchors: refs.slice(), anchor: refs[0],
                  source: "concept:" + b.concept };
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    });
    return found || { anchors: [], anchor: null, source: null };
  }
```

Add this helper inside the IIFE, immediately above `toJSONLD`:

```js
  /*
   * prov:wasQuotedFrom takes a list now that a use can rest on several passages.
   * An array of quotation nodes is better JSON-LD than the single node it
   * replaces — the relation was always many-valued in PROV.

  function quotationNodes(refs, docIri) {

- [ ] **Step 8: Make `allAnchors` walk lists**

In `smartphrase/tools/lib-anchors.mjs`, replace `allAnchors` (lines 75–92):

```js
export function allAnchors(graph) {
  const out = [];
  const addAll = (where, refs) => {
    if (!Array.isArray(refs)) return;
    refs.forEach((a, i) => {
      if (a && typeof a === "object" && a.section) {
        out.push({ where: refs.length > 1 ? `${where} ref[${i}]` : where, ...a });
      }
    });
  };

  Object.keys(graph.concepts || {}).forEach((id) =>
    addAll(`concept ${id}`, graph.concepts[id].sapRefs));
  Object.keys(graph.estimands || {}).forEach((id) =>
    addAll(`estimand ${id}`, graph.estimands[id].sapRefs));

  (graph.instances || []).forEach((inst) => {
    addAll(`instance ${inst.id}`, inst.sapRefs);
    (inst.phrases || []).forEach((pi, i) => {
      addAll(`${inst.id} phrase[${i}] ${pi.phrase}`, pi.sapRefs);
    });
  });
  return out;
}
```

Also update the module's header comment, replacing the line `An anchor is \`{ section, quote? }\` on a study-side entity` with:

```

 * carries a LIST of them (issue #13) — a concept reused across analyses whose
 * specifying text lives in different sections needs more than one.
```

## Task 2: Union resolution with proximity and relation ranking

Replace first-match-wins with collect-all-and-rank. Study data still holds one reference per site, so live prose does not move; the new behaviour is proven on probes and on the projections.

**Files:**
- Modify: `smartphrase/demo/engine.js` — the comment block and body at lines 228–254, `resolvePhrase` signature and return, `resolveInstance` call site (line 301), `constructModelView` `documentAnchors`, `toJSONLD` phrase-node call
- Modify: `smartphrase/tools/verify.mjs` — new ranking block

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `refsOf(x)` and `anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def)` from Task 1.
- Produces:
  - `sectionProximity(a, b) → Number` — count of matching leading dotted components
  - `rankAnchors(cands, contextSection) → Array` — `cands` are `{ ref, level, from }`; returns them ordered, each gaining `_prox` and `_rel`
  - `anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def, instance) → { anchors, anchor, source, basis, contextSection }` where each entry of `anchors` is the authored ref plus `from` (String) and `proximity` (Number)
  - `resolvePhrase(ctx, pi, lang, tpl, instance)` — fifth parameter optional; resolved phrases gain `anchorBasis` and `anchorContextSection`
  - Model view `documentAnchors[]` entries: `{ phrase, role, section, quote, relation, from, proximity, head, basis }`

 * Study data still holds one reference per site at this point, so these run on

{

    E.resolveInstance(ctx, i, "en").phrases.find((p) => p.role === "endpoint");

     the count resolved must now equal the count authored. */

  ctxTwo.graph.concepts["EVENT.PFS"].sapRefs = [
    { section: "5.3", quote: "the duration of time from time of randomization to time of progression or death, whichever occurs first" },
    { section: "7.7.2", quote: "PFS = time from randomization to documented disease progression or death" }
  ];
  const rTwo = E.resolveInstance(ctxTwo, inst, "en").phrases.find((p) => p.role === "endpoint");

  /* PROXIMITY. The instance is specified at 7.7.2, so the 7.7.2 reference must

  check("the nearer reference leads",
    rTwo.anchor.section === "7.7.2", JSON.stringify(rTwo.anchor));
  check("the engine reports proximity as the basis",
    rTwo.anchorBasis === "proximity", String(rTwo.anchorBasis));
  check("the engine reports the section it measured against",
    rTwo.anchorContextSection === "7.7.2", String(rTwo.anchorContextSection));

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the ranking primitives to `engine.js`**

Insert immediately above the `refsOf` function added in Task 1:

```js
  /*
   * Relation ranks (issue #13). Unlabelled sits in the MIDDLE deliberately:
   * labelling a reference `specification` promotes it and labelling it
   * `definition` demotes it, and both are positive claims an author has made.
   * `qualification` sits just above unlabelled because a caveat attached to
   * this analysis is more use-specific than a passage nobody has characterised.
   *
   * No registered identifier covers "why this passage grounds this use" —
   * USDM, ARS, STATO and NCIt are all silent — so the vocabulary is
   * illustrative under the project's identifier policy, and deliberately stops
   * at three terms.
   */
  var RELATION_RANK = { specification: 0, qualification: 1, definition: 3 };
  var RELATION_NEUTRAL = 2;

  /*
   * How near a reference is to the section that specifies the analysis being
   * inspected: the number of matching leading dotted components. Against
   * "7.7.2", a "7.7.2" reference scores 3, "7.2" scores 1, and "5.3" scores 0.
   *
   * This assumes dotted section numbering. A document anchored by heading text
   * alone scores every reference 0 and falls through to relation, then
   * declaration order — a stated limitation, not a silent one.
   */
  function sectionProximity(a, b) {
    if (!a || !b) return 0;
    var x = String(a).split("."), y = String(b).split(".");
    var n = 0;
    while (n < x.length && n < y.length && x[n] === y[n]) n++;
    return n;
  }

  /* Enough normalisation to spot the same passage reached by two routes. The
     gate's normaliser (tools/lib-anchors.mjs) is stricter because it compares
     against the document; this one only has to catch duplicates. */
  function anchorKey(ref) {
    return ref.section + "|" +
      String(ref.quote || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim().toLowerCase();
  }

  /*
   * Order candidates by, outermost key first: level (a use-specific anchor
   * outranks a definitional one — issue #12's decision, unchanged), then
   * proximity, then relation, then declaration order. Declaration order is the
   * LAST resort; it used to be the first, which is the bug.
   */
  function rankAnchors(cands, contextSection) {
    return cands.map(function (c, i) {
      var rel = RELATION_RANK[c.ref.relation];
      return {
        ref: c.ref, level: c.level, from: c.from,
        _prox: sectionProximity(c.ref.section, contextSection),
        _rel: rel === undefined ? RELATION_NEUTRAL : rel,
        _i: i
      };
    }).sort(function (a, b) {
      return a.level - b.level || b._prox - a._prox || a._rel - b._rel || a._i - b._i;
    });
  }

  /* What actually distinguished the head from the runner-up, so a heuristic is
     never presented to a reviewer as a stated fact. Named basisOf rather than
     anchorBasis because the resolved phrase carries a FIELD of that name. */
  function basisOf(ordered) {
    if (!ordered.length) return null;
    if (ordered.length === 1) return "only";
    var a = ordered[0], b = ordered[1];
    if (a.level !== b.level) return "level";
    if (a._prox !== b._prox) return "proximity";
    if (a._rel !== b._rel) return "relation";
    return "declarationOrder";
  }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Replace `anchorForPhrase` with the union resolver**

Replace the whole comment block and function at lines 228–254 (as left by Task 1) with:

```js
  /*
   * Every document reference that grounds one phrase USE, ordered by relevance
   * to the analysis being inspected (issues #12 and #13).
   *
   * #12 gave a use a path back to the document. #13 is that ONE path was not
   * enough: a concept exists to be reused, its definitional quote sits wherever
   * it was first defined, and first-match-wins then sent every later analysis
   * to that same passage instead of to the text specifying it. An independent
   * reviewer working through 96 encoded instances hit this repeatedly.
   *
   * So: collect from the phrase instance and from every bound concept,
   * deduplicate, and rank. The instance's own anchor is the REFERENCE POINT for
   * proximity, never a member of the set — admitting it would make every use
   * resolve to something and turn the declared-empty rule into a dead letter.
   *
   * Shared by resolvePhrase and toJSONLD so the prose and the graph cannot
   * disagree, and so neither has to pair a resolved phrase back to its instance
   * by oid — which would break for a repeating role using one oid twice.
   */
  function anchorForPhrase(ctx, pi, def, instance) {
    var contextSection = (refsOf(instance)[0] || {}).section || null;
    var cands = [];
    refsOf(pi).forEach(function (r) {
      cands.push({ ref: r, level: 0, from: "phraseInstance" });
    });
    ((def && def.placeholders) || []).forEach(function (ph) {
      var b = (pi.bindings || {})[ph.name];
      var c = b && b.concept && concept(ctx, b.concept);
      refsOf(c).forEach(function (r) {
        cands.push({ ref: r, level: 1, from: "concept:" + b.concept });
      });
    });

    var seen = {};
    var uniq = cands.filter(function (c) {
      var k = anchorKey(c.ref);
      if (seen[k]) return false;
      seen[k] = true;
      return true;
    });

    var ordered = rankAnchors(uniq, contextSection);
    var head = ordered[0] || null;
    return {
      anchors: ordered.map(function (o) {
        return Object.assign({}, o.ref, { from: o.from, proximity: o._prox });
      }),
      anchor: head ? head.ref : null,
      source: head ? head.from : null,
      basis: basisOf(ordered),
      contextSection: contextSection,
      declaredEmpty: Array.isArray(pi.sapRefs) && pi.sapRefs.length === 0
    };
  }
```

Those two new entries are the union resolver working, not a regression. `ICE.TOX_DISCONT` is the one site in either study where a concept and the phrase instance binding it both carry their own reference — both in §4.3, but different sentences: the phrase cites *"All subjects who have discontinued protocol therapy will be followed for survival and for progression…"*, which justifies the treatment-policy handling, while the concept cites *"Subjects who discontinue everolimus/placebo because of suspected everolimus-associated toxicity…"*, which defines the event. The data file's own comment says as much: *"Same section, different claim."* First-match-wins discarded the concept's sentence silently — the issue's third failure mode, "secondary anchors invisible", live in this repo.

So the constraint is: **no `section` value may change, and no entry may be removed.** Entries may be *added* exactly where a previously-discarded reference now surfaces, and every addition must be explicable as one. An unexplained addition, or any removal or changed section value, means the ranker is being applied where there was nothing to rank — stop and investigate.

    /*
     * The row issue #12 exists for, made plural by #13. Before #12, hovering a
     * method, value or output phrase showed no path back to the document at all
     * — those bindings resolve into the library, which correctly forbids study
     * text — and a fixed-text phrase had no binding to route through. Before

     * be authored first.

    function anchorLevel(a) {
      return a.from === "phraseInstance"
        ? "the phrase use" : "the bound concept (" + a.from.replace("concept:", "") + ")";
    }
    function anchorWhy(rp) {
      var head = rp.anchors[0];
      if (rp.anchorBasis === "proximity") {
        return "nearest to SAP " + rp.anchorContextSection +
               ", the section specifying this analysis";
      }
      if (rp.anchorBasis === "relation") {
        return "the " + head.relation + " for this analysis";
      }
      return "anchored at " + anchorLevel(head);
    }
    var src = "";
    if ((rp.anchors || []).length) {
      var head = rp.anchors[0];
      var rest = rp.anchors.slice(1);
      src = "<tr><td class='k'>source</td><td><b>SAP " + head.section + "</b>" +
        (head.relation ? "<span class='relbadge'>" + head.relation + "</span>" : "") +
        (head.quote ? "<div class='quote'>“" + head.quote + "”</div>" : "") +
        "<div class='anchorfrom'>" + anchorWhy(rp) + " · from " + anchorLevel(head) + "</div>" +
        (rest.length
          ? "<div class='alsoref'>also grounded in " +
            rest.map(function (a) {
              return "<b>SAP " + a.section + "</b>" +
                     (a.relation ? " (" + a.relation + ")" : "");
            }).join(", ") + "</div>"
          : "") +
        "</td></tr>";
    } else if (rp.anchorDeclaredEmpty) {
      src = "<tr><td class='k'>source</td><td><span class='noanchor'>" +
        "nothing in the document to anchor to — declared</span></td></tr>";
    }

- [ ] **Step 2: Rewrite `REFERENCE.md` §3.4**

The section currently describes a single `{ section, quote? }` per entity. Replace the anchor-shape description with this, keeping the declared-empty subsection Task 4 already added:

```markdown
An anchor is `{ section, quote?, relation? }`, and every study-side home carries
a **list** of them — concepts, phrase instances, estimands and analysis
instances:

```js
sapRefs: [
  { section: "5.3",   quote: "…", relation: "definition" },
  { section: "7.7.2", quote: "…", relation: "specification" }
]
```

A concept exists to be reused, and the analyses that bind it are specified in
different sections, so one reference cannot be the right anchor for all of them.

`relation` is optional and takes one of three values: `specification` (this
passage specifies this analysis), `qualification` (a condition or caveat on it),
`definition` (background — it defines the entity without specifying the
analysis). No registry covers this relation, so the vocabulary is
**illustrative** and stops at three terms.

**Resolution.** A phrase use's references are the union of its own and those of
every concept it binds, deduplicated on section plus quote, ordered by:

1. **level** — a reference on the phrase instance outranks one on a bound
   concept, because it answers *"why is this here?"* rather than *"what is
   this?"*;
2. **proximity** — the number of matching leading dotted components against the
   analysis's own section. Against §7.7.2, a §7.7.2 reference scores 3, §7.2
   scores 1, §5.3 scores 0;
3. **relation** — breaking a proximity tie only, ranked `specification`,
   `qualification`, unlabelled, `definition`;
4. **declaration order** — the last resort. It used to be the only key.

`anchorBasis` reports which of these chose the leading reference, so a heuristic
is never presented as a stated fact.

The analysis instance's own anchor is the **reference point** proximity is
measured against — it is never a member of a phrase's reference set. Admitting
it would make every use resolve to something, and the declared-empty rule below
would never fire.

Proximity assumes dotted section numbering. A document anchored by heading text
alone scores every reference 0 and falls through to relation, then declaration
order.

Every reference is projected: `sapRefs[]` and `documentAnchors[]` in the model
view, and `prov:wasQuotedFrom` as an **array** of quotation nodes in the graph.
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Append the design decisions to `DESIGN.md`**

Append after D18, in the file's `**Dnn — Title.**` format (verify D18 is the highest first — Step 1). Write these three entries, expanding each into the file's usual two or three paragraphs of prose:

**D19 — Anchors are plural at every study-side home; the singular field is gone.**
Cover: one quote per concept cannot serve analyses specified in different sections; #12 established the four homes and this widens each to a list; back-compatibility with a singular `sapRef` was offered by the issue and declined, because all authoring is in-repo and dual-shape support is gate surface forever; absent and empty are different answers.

**D20 — Relevance is section proximity, with an optional authored relation as tie-break; declaration order is the last key, not the first.**
Cover: the bug was that binding order — an authoring accident — decided which passage a reviewer saw; proximity is *derivable*, so it repairs an existing corpus with no re-authoring, which is what the issue's acceptance sketch actually asks for; a fully typed vocabulary was the honest alternative but would require touching all 96 instances before the reviewer's problem improved; **level stays the outermost key**, so #12's precedence decision is preserved unchanged — concretely, `SP_ICE_TREATMENT_POLICY`'s deliberate §4.3 anchor is not demoted by a nearer §7.7.2 concept reference; and the engine reports the basis so proximity is never mistaken for a stated fact.

**D21 — A use grounded in no passage must declare it; the instance's own anchor is the proximity reference point, not a member of the set.**
Cover: silence could not be distinguished from "nothing to anchor to", which is one of the three failure modes the reviewer hit; the same discipline #11 chose for `Estimand.intercurrentEvents`, cross-reference [[D16]]-style to that decision; and the reason the instance anchor is excluded from the set — including it would make every use resolve to something and turn this rule into a dead letter on the day it was written.

Also state in D20 what was deliberately *not* changed: the four `SP_GROUPING` uses still cite §4.1, because that reference is correct and the only §7.7.2 fragment available recurs throughout the section. The fix is for references that are wrong, not for every reference that is distant.
